scope: Explicit user-authorized unavailable-capability boundaries; not successful implementations of native effects or complete BIF-batch acceptance.
adaptations: The exact 27 erlang MFAs classified as whole-MFA denials in bif-batch-contracts.json have explicit native entries. These deliberately do not execute their upstream bodies or validate effectful-wrapper arguments. Unknown/unclassified imports remain eager load-time failures. No generic fallback is added.

A denial charges one primitive unit, allocates nothing and stores only a static bounded MFA/capability descriptor. Work failure before the entry charge remains work failure. Distinct process/task/World/public error categories bypass guest exception and guard paths.

The single worker records denial on its retained causal budget before destroying the offender, suppresses guest monitor notification, fails a pending owning call, and cancels private siblings or closes an escaped World according to existing causal containment. Completed responses are not rewritten. Diagnostics survive process/code/World-storage reclamation.

Native ops.tab lowers direct load_nif/2 to i_load_nif. Its entire prohibited operation is replaced with the same reviewed denial before code-modification permission or library access. Dynamic calls use the corresponding native export. This is a policy override, not a claim to preserve successful NIF behavior.

Native emu_load.c elides nif_start metadata; the owned loader does likewise after a verified function header, including compiler placement after allocate/init prologues. No heap/register proof is created. No NIF patch table is needed because installation remains prohibited; actual call_nif instructions, on_load, and unimplemented padding remain refused.

Thirteen denied preloaded-wrapper arities receive owned extension IDs after the five existing conversion entries. set_cookie is appended to immutable predefined names without shifting original indices; the pinned naming inputs and generator remain unchanged.

Focused tests cover all 27 direct and dynamic calls, zero/exact/extra primitive work under quota/callback denial, no allocation/atom/root changes, monitored child propagation, private reuse, escaped World closure, live peer and replacement, static diagnostic lifetime and allocator balance, and public C++ error identity/consumption. Admitted catch/rescue tests, further resource prefixes and full batch validation remain pending.
